items.excerpt: ## Political Gridlock in Israel After No Clear Winner Emerges from Tuesday’s National Election Oct 28, 2026 In Israel, there’s no clear winner so far in Tuesday’s national election. The final tally could take days. It was Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023, attack and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. With over 70% of the vote counted, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party leads with 27 seats, ahead of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party at 22. Neither candidate is on track to form a governing majority of 61 seats in the Knesset. According to Haaretz, a possible pro-Netanyahu coalition currently has 54 seats, while a possible pro-Eisenkot bloc has 49 seats. Palestinian parties — the Joint List and Ra’am — have won 17 seats, their strongest showing ever. But both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have ruled out governing with Palestinian-led parties. Meanwhile, millions of Palestinians living under Israeli occupation in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza were ineligible to vote. This is Netanyahu speaking on Tuesday.

items.title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
items.excerpt: ## Press Release October 28, 2026 ### Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability. Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

items.title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh’s Press Conference - October 28, 2026
items.excerpt: Transcript of Chairman Warsh’s Press Conference Opening Statement October 28, 2026 CHAIRMAN WARSH. Good day. This morning the FOMC decided to maintain the target rate for the federal funds rate at 3¾ to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve’s dual mandate. Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains—owing, in part, to geopolitical developments—domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. But inflation remains elevated. The Committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability. At each policy meeting, my colleagues and I assess the economy by looking out the window—it’s what we call “interrogating reality”—to gauge what’s really going on. It is not a task that has grown easier. So what exactly do we observe? Economic growth has strengthened. The GDP increase in the first half of this year was revised up from an earlier estimate of 1.8 percent up to 2.4 percent. And the third quarter appears to have brought an even more rapid advance, led by healthy consumer spending, likely running above 3 percent growth, and business investment, likely rising at about a double-digit pace. Capital expenditures are at a historically high share of GDP. High-tech investment is leading the acceleration. But there’s also been a broadening in other categories. And these trends bear watching. What about the jobless rate? The jobless rate is lower than a year ago, and payroll growth is noticeably above last year’s pace. The four-week moving average of unemployment insurance claims continues to run at the lowest level in generations. So on the employment side of the Fed’s dual mandate, conditions are quite positive. And yet Americans, of course, are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the Committee’s objective for close to 6 years. It’s our responsibility to get inflation down. That’s the reason the FOMC’s discussion over the last couple of days focused mainly on the price stability side of our remit. Since our policy action in September, we have started to see some changes in financial and credit conditions. They have tightened for some businesses and households, much as we would expect. Market participants are becoming somewhat more discerning in their capital allocations. And while overall financial conditions are tighter, I’m unwilling and unable to call them tight. But broadly, these developments go in the direction of achieving a longer, more durable period of economic growth and price stability. Over the last couple of days, the Committee had a good discussion of the changes in the economic and financial landscape that marked this inter-meeting period. We discussed geopolitical developments and fast-moving changes in technology. We observed—but were not surprised—that financial markets showed bouts of volatility and shifting correlations. So as we widen the frame to survey the broad economic and financial picture, real activity is clearly pointing in the right direction. That’s good news. But inflation is too high. Energy and related prices have moved higher again in recent weeks. And our job is to ensure that relative price changes in some sectors do not broaden out across the economy, and that inflation expectations remain as they are anchored.

items.title: Fed keeps interest rates steady despite rising inflation
items.excerpt: Oct. 28, 2026, 2:01 PM EDT / Updated Oct. 28, 2026, 2:44 PM EDT By Steve Kopack, Maya Huter and Brian Cheung The Federal Reserve on Wednesday voted to keep interest rates unchanged, its final monetary policy decision before the midterm elections. The decision to hold rates steady came despite inflation that jumped from a 3.4% annual rate in August to 3.7% in September. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh also announced that the central bank will reduce the number of meetings at which it votes on interest rates from eight to seven next year and by two in 2028. Warsh said that the seismic change to the schedule would help improve the “quality” of its decisions. A major driver of that inflation is the soaring cost of gas, diesel and crude oil. These higher prices have hit consumers hard, and many economists say the spillover effect of rising gas prices has started to show up across the broader economy. In its post-decision statement, the Fed acknowledged the problem that inflation is causing but said it needs more data before moving forward with a rate hike. “Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s 2 percent goal,” it said. The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, will not be released until Thursday, but it is expected to touch 3.7%.

items.title: Live Updates: 2026 midterm campaigns make final push before Election Day as early voters hit the polls
items.excerpt: Updated on: October 28, 2026 / 4:02 PM EDT / CBS News ## What to know leading up to Election Day 2026 - Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and early voting is currently underway throughout the country. More than 36 million people have voted early as of Wednesday morning, according to the University of Florida Election Lab. - All 435 House seats plus 35 Senate seats will be on the ballot, and voters in 36 states will be electing governors. - CBS News' Battleground Tracker estimates that Democrats have an edge in the race for control of the House. Senate control could be decided by voters in a handful of toss-up states ranging from Alaska to Maine. - President Trump heads to Ohio today to campaign for GOP Sen. Jon Husted and Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for governor, part of a weekslong blitz that brought him to Texas on Tuesday and Mississippi on Monday. ... ## Ted Cruz calls Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist leprechaun," as GOP closing message leans into attacks Grosse Pointe Woods, Michigan — At a campaign event outside of Detroit, GOP Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas attempted to tie Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood — a claim El-Sayed has repeatedly denied. "My nickname for the guy is the jihadist leprechaun," Cruz said about El-Sayed. Cruz later said that El-Sayed would get top-level security clearance as a U.S. Senator if elected, claiming that El-Sayed could be put on the Senate Intelligence Committee, "and if I am correct that he is a passionate supporter of the Muslim Brotherhood, there is a very real risk that Americans will die as a result." The insinuation El-Sayed has ties with the Muslim Brotherhood has been a core part of the closing message for Republican nominee Mike Rogers in what is expected to be a razor-tight Senate race in Michigan. Some branches of the group were designated as a terrorist organization by the Trump administration in January. El-Sayed said in a recent interview with Fox News: "I have never been a member of the Muslim Brotherhood, I never will be a member of the Muslim Brotherhood." ... ## Murkowski backs Democratic candidate for governor Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who has bucked President Trump and the GOP, on Tuesday backed the Democratic candidate for governor in Alaska, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, who is widely referred to as JKT. "JKT is a young Alaskan with a view and a perspective that I think Alaska needs right now," Murkowski told Anchorage's KTUU-TV on Tuesday. She said Kriess-Tomkins will "work with the legislature," adding that will be important for the state's at-large representative and senators in Washington, D.C. In a news release, Murkowski encouraged "Alaskans of every political stripe, whether Republicans, independents, or Democrats" to consider Kriess-Tomkins, adding "Alaska needs leaders who will put our state first, and I'm proud to support them." Murkowski said she has "found fault" with the current GOP Gov. Mike Dunleavy's administration. Dunleavy is prevented from running for reelection due to term limits. "I think that they have left federal money on the table," Murkowski said of Dunleavy. "I think in certain areas, where we have worked hard to put opportunities from the federal side, here, into the state, the state has failed with it." Kriess-Tomkins has three Republican challengers on the ballot on Nov. 3, and Alaska uses ranked-choice voting. In a statement, Kriess-Tomkins, who has touted bipartisanship on the trail, said he was "honored to have Senator Murkowski's support." ... ## 47 battleground House seats could determine which party wins control Control of the House of Representatives will come down to a number of battleground seats. CBS News has identified 47 House districts that will likely determine which party will have the majority. Of those seats, 20 are currently held by Democrats and 27 are held by Republicans. Republicans currently hold a razor-thin majority, with 218 seats, plus an independent who normally caucuses with them. Democrats hold 214 seats. There are two vacancies. CBS News' Battleground Tracker model estimated on Sunday that Democrats are on track to take control of the House with 229 seats. There is still a path for the GOP to keep the House: The Battleground Tracker's estimates ranged from 215 Democratic seats — which would give Republicans a narrow majority — to 237 seats.

items.excerpt: UK's Channel 4 shows to launch on Disney+ next year Channel 4 has signed a deal with ​The Walt Disney Company to bring its shows to the Disney+ streaming platform in Britain and Ireland ​early next year. The collaboration will see many of Channel 4's programmes, including ‌drama "Maya", ​featuring Bella Ramsey, released on Disney+ at the same time as on Channel 4's own platforms, the broadcaster said on Tuesday. Actor Walter Koenig, 'Star Trek's' plucky Chekov, dies at 90 Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature ‌films, has died at the age of 90. "My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today," George Takei, who starred alongside Koenig in the show and was a long-time friend, wrote on Facebook on Monday. Koenig died at his home in Los Angeles, the AP reported, citing his talent agent. Meghan to join Australia's Junior MasterChef next year Meghan, the wife of Britain's Prince Harry, will star in the next series of Australia's Junior MasterChef in ‌2027, returning to a franchise where she appeared as a guest judge on the adult version earlier this year. Meghan, an American actress before she married Harry in 2018, has recently moved back to Britain from the US ‌with her family, with media reports suggesting she was keen to find a new acting role. Noah Wyle named People magazine's 'sexiest man alive' Actor Noah Wyle, the Emmy-winning star of the TV medical drama “The Pitt,” was named this year’s “sexiest man alive” by People magazine on Tuesday. The 55-year-old said it “sounded like a prank” when he heard the news, adding: “Not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me.” Universal Music Group discussed going private with buyout firms, Bloomberg News reports Universal Music Group held preliminary discussions with private equity firms earlier ⁠this year ​about going private, Bloomberg News reported on Monday, citing people familiar ⁠with the matter. The music label's management held preliminary talks with private equity firms including Apollo Global Management, TPG and Blackstone, according to the report ... Macklemore vows to fight until 'last breath' ⁠at opening of 'Free Palestine' tour American rapper Macklemore vowed to continue to speak out loudly against Israel's war in Gaza at the opening of his "Free Palestine" concert tour organised after he was dropped as the opening act for ⁠Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks. The Grammy-winning rapper received a deafening ⁠ovation in Dublin, where fans in the overwhelmingly pro-Palestinian country came draped in Palestinian flags, black, red and green football jerseys and keffiyeh scarves being sold by vendors outside.

items.excerpt: - Oct 28, 2026 - Oct 28, 2026 Updated 22 mins ago Ken Burns wins a $250,000 prize for bringing American history to life NEW YORK (AP) — Ken Burns has won a $250,000 prize for his contributions to American history. The New York Historical awarded him the inaugural David M. Rubenstein Prize for the Advancement of American History. The jury praised Burns for his work on topics like the American Revolution and the Civil War. They noted his films have brought the history of the U.S. to more people than perhaps any other single body of work. Burns expressed gratitude, acknowledging the collective effort of historians and archivists. The award was established earlier this year by financier David M. Rubenstein. California appeals court upholds actor Danny Masterson's rape convictions LOS ANGELES (AP) — A California appeals court has upheld actor Danny Masterson’s convictions and long prison sentence for raping two women at his home in 2003. The three-judge panel on Tuesday unanimously found that the “That ’70s Show” actor had failed to demonstrate that the lower court made errors that would warrant granting him a new trial. Masterson was convicted in 2023 of raping two women at his home two decades earlier. He was sentenced to 30 years to life in prison. His attorneys said in an emailed statement Tuesday that they would seek review at the California Supreme Court. Russell Brand denies all charges as he takes the stand at his rape and sex assault trial LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand says allegations of sexual misconduct have had a “devastating” impact on his life. The actor and comedian testified in court Wednesday at his trial on charges of rape and sexual assault. Brand, 51, denied all charges, stating that friends and colleagues have abandoned him. He also mentioned being barred from staying with his baby son in the hospital due to the allegations. Over the past two weeks, prosecutors have presented their case, with six women accusing Brand of misconduct between 1999 and 2009. Brand insists that consent is fundamental, denying any wrongdoing. Iran sentences acclaimed film director Jafar Panahi to new prison term after his return home CAIRO (AP) — Iran has sentenced acclaimed film director Jafar Panahi to five years and one month in prison, following his return to the country earlier this year, after the start of U.S. and Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic. The Tehran court also ordered the confiscation of Panahi’s “movable and immovable assets.” That's according to his lawyer Mostafa Nili, who spoke in an interview with the reformist news site Emtedad on Tuesday. Nili did not say what Panahi was convicted of. But the director, who returned to Iran in March, had been previously convicted of “propaganda activities against the system.” Susan Saint James, Emmy-winning actor of 'McMillan & Wife' and 'Kate & Allie,' dies at 80 LOS ANGELES (AP) — Susan Saint James, known for her roles in “McMillan & Wife” and “Kate & Allie,” has died at 80. People magazine reports she passed away Monday after a battle with pancreatic cancer. Born in Los Angeles, she started modeling in Paris as a teenager and later signed with Universal Studios. She gained fame in the 1970s and 1980s, earning multiple Emmy nominations. Saint James retired to focus on family but occasionally appeared on TV. She was a longtime supporter of the Special Olympics and leaves behind her husband, children, and extended family. Taylor Swift, Lyle Lovett and more inducted into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Taylor Swift has been inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, alongside Lyle Lovett, Shawn Camp, Lee Thomas Miller, Bruce Channel and J.I. Allison. Swift signed her first publishing deal in Nashville at the age of 14. She returned to the city on Monday during the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame annual gala celebration. She said it was an incredible honor to be inducted and described soaking up the lessons from other writers like a sponge. Also honored was country music icon George Strait with the organization's Career Maker Award. He said the songwriters helped to make his career. Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show at SoFi Stadium in Southern California LOS ANGELES (AP) — Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl halftime show on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The NFL, Apple Music, and Roc Nation announced the news Monday night. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he always wanted Jay-Z to perform when the time felt right. Jay-Z expressed excitement about the opportunity, calling it a dream come true. His Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to produce entertainment presentations, including the halftime show. Jay-Z, who has won 25 Grammy Awards, will perform at the stadium where he recently celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.” Andrea Bocelli concerts in Indonesia to proceed despite opposition from Muslim clerics JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli's concerts in Indonesia will proceed despite opposition from the country's top Muslim clerical body. The Indonesian Ulema Council demanded the cancellation due to Bocelli's past support for Israel. Indonesia, a strong supporter of Palestinians, does not have formal diplomatic relations with Israel. The concerts are scheduled for October 31 at Borobudur Temple and November 3 in Jakarta. Promoter Shoemaker Live insists the events will support Indonesia's tourism and culture sectors. Bocelli plans to dedicate songs to humanity and world peace. The council argues the concerts could hurt Indonesians who support Palestinians. After pushback, the Dutch reverse course and withdraw from Eurovision again AMSTERDAM (AP) — The Netherlands is withdrawing from participating in the Eurovision Song Contest, reversing a decision in September to return to the show. NPO, the umbrella organization for public broadcasters in the country announced in September it would send a performer to the event, after a subsidiary had said a month earlier it would boycott the contest for a second year. Earlier this month, hundreds of NPO employees sent a letter opposing Dutch participation. A number of prominent Dutch media personalities also publicly objected to the move.
